entities.summary:
Hyecho (혜초, 704–787 CE) was an eminent Silla Korean Buddhist monk and intrepid traveler whose seven-year pilgrimage across Central Asia and India profoundly illuminated the state of Buddhism and geopolitical dynamics of the 8th-century Silk Road. His comprehensive travelogue, the *Wang Ocheonchukguk Jeon* (Account of a Journey to the Five Indian Kingdoms), offers an unparalleled firsthand perspective on the diverse cultures, religious practices, and political landscapes from the Korean peninsula to the heartlands of Buddhism. Active during a period of intense cultural exchange between East Asia and the Indian subcontinent, Hyecho’s journey bridged the spiritual and geographical divides, making him a crucial primary source for understanding medieval Asian history and the transmission of Buddhist thought.

Departing from Tang China around 723 CE, Hyecho embarked on an arduous overland journey, traversing the perilous mountains and deserts of Central Asia, including regions corresponding to modern Afghanistan, Pakistan, and Uzbekistan. He spent several years meticulously documenting his observations throughout the Indian subcontinent, visiting numerous Buddhist holy sites, monasteries, and kingdoms, from Kashmir in the north to the southern reaches of India, before returning to China via the maritime route. His detailed narrative captures the decline of Buddhism in some Indian regions alongside its flourishing in others, providing invaluable details on local customs, languages, and political rivalries, such as the power struggles between various Hindu and Buddhist polities. Upon his return to Chang'an, the Tang capital, around 727 CE, Hyecho dedicated himself to translating Sanskrit sutras into Chinese, contributing directly to the East Asian Buddhist canon.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hyecho's travelogue offers a unique and invaluable primary source for understanding the geopolitical and religious landscape of 8th-century Central and South Asia, providing details unavailable from other contemporary records. His journey exemplifies the intense cultural and religious exchanges along the Silk Road, influencing East Asian Buddhist scholarship.
